title: Jaylen Warren Earns First AFC Offensive Player of the Week Honor, Sparks Broncos’ Momentum
body:
Pittsburgh’s running back Jaylen Warren captured the AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor on Sunday after delivering a career‑defining performance that helped the Steelers dominate the Indianapolis Colts 31‑17. Warren rushed for a franchise‑record 188 yards on 23 carries, scoring two touchdowns and breaking several tackles en route to a night that not only turned the tide of the game but also signaled his emergence as a cornerstone of Pittsburgh’s offense.

The Steelers entered the contest as underdogs, having dropped two of their last three outings and struggling to establish a consistent ground attack. Their rushing game had been largely a revolving door, with veteran James Conner limited by injuries and rookie Kenny Pickett’s passing attempts failing to produce sustained drives. Against that backdrop, Warren’s explosive burst early in the first quarter set a new rhythm for the team. He burst through a gap on the opening drive and sprinted 42 yards for a touchdown, instantly putting the Steelers ahead and forcing the Colts to play from behind for the first time all season.

Warren’s performance was not a flash in the pan; it was the culmination of a steady progression that began when he was drafted in the fourth round last year. After a modest rookie season in which he served primarily as a backup, he earned increased snaps in the preseason and capitalized on injuries to the depth chart. His 188 yards on the day eclipsed his previous best of 112, a mark set earlier this season against the Buffalo Bills, and placed him among the top single‑game rushers in Steelers history. The two touchdowns—one a 42‑yard dash and the other a 15‑yard plunge from the goal line—demonstrated his versatility, showing that he can break long runs as well as power through short‑yardage situations.

The impact of Warren’s breakout extended beyond the stat sheet. By establishing a reliable rushing threat, the Steelers were able to balance their offense, allowing Pickett to stay in the pocket longer and reduce the number of forced throws that had plagued the team in recent weeks. The offensive line, anchored by veteran guard Maurkice Poe, opened more running lanes than they had all season, and Warren’s vision and acceleration turned those openings into big gains. Defensive coordinator Keith Mayo noted after the game that the ground game forced the Colts to respect the run, opening up play‑action opportunities that ultimately led to a crucial interception in the fourth quarter.

Colts coach Shane Stewart tried to adjust, stacking the box and daring Pickett to beat the Steelers through the air. While Indianapolis managed a couple of short passing scores, they never regained momentum, largely because Warren’s relentless pounding kept the clock moving and the Colts’ defense on the field. The Steelers’ secondary also stepped up, forcing three incompletions and a fumble that set up a field goal, further cementing the team’s dominance in all three phases of the game.

Looking ahead, Warren’s accolade could herald a shift in Pittsburgh’s offensive identity. With Conner’s health still uncertain and the team’s draft capital limited, the Steelers may lean more heavily on a younger, high‑upside back who has already shown the ability to carry a workload of 20+ carries per game without a dip in productivity. If Warren can maintain this level of performance, he could become the focal point of a revamped run‑centric scheme that complements Pickett’s growing poise under center. The AFC Offensive Player of the Week award not only rewards a single night of brilliance but also underscores a potential turning point for a Steelers franchise eager to return to playoff contention.
